scope: Cross-tab manual-presence preference synchronization and safeguards against stale automatic presence transitions leaking hidden or DND state.
implemented: Presence broadcasts carry an explicit is_auto boolean, including false for manual changes. Receiving clients sync their local manualStatus only for an explicit false self event; automatic or legacy events update displayed user status without persisting a manual preference. This propagates manual preference updates to open tabs.

Automatic presence callbacks reload persisted pref_status before writing or broadcasting; they ignore late automatic updates when the preferred status is not online. This protects DND and manual idle from stale tab activity.
The callback uses Hub.IsInvisible, a single-lock Hub getter, and refuses automatic non-offline status changes while hidden. Manual status selection alone may reveal a hidden account.
Manual visible status changes update/persist preference and visibility before the online-friend notifier runs; automatic changes do not trigger that manual notifier path.

Presence callback ordering is implemented_unverified: the bounded WebSocket dispatcher enforces same-user FIFO completion while allowing cross-user progress, and protects Hub visibility commits from stale callbacks. See p6-presence-callback-order-2026-10-24.json for repeated/race/PostgreSQL checks and remaining gates.

open_gates: The dispatcher preserves per-user callback FIFO, but broader semantic outcomes under rapid interleaved manual and automatic updates still require real two-client/device acceptance.
The server event's status value is an account-wide aggregate across connections; source-tab intent versus that aggregate still needs explicit multi-device semantics and validation.

A callback that never returns cannot be canceled globally and may delay dispatcher shutdown; relevant database callback operations are generally bounded by five-second contexts but this is not a universal cancellation guarantee.
